cr_baslik: AI CoRider — the riding partner in your helmet | Motoseyir
cr_og_baslik: AI CoRider: eyes on the road, it listens
cr_aciklama: Motoseyir’s AI CoRider talks to you through your helmet: it adds stops, finds places on your route, checks weather and fuel range, and changes the route for you.
cr_lead: AI CoRider is the riding partner who talks to you through your helmet headset. It knows your route: it adds stops, finds places along the way and changes the route for you. Press the button, ask in your own words, and hear the answer in your helmet. Your hands stay on the bars.
cr_micro: A Pro feature. You can also buy minute packs that never expire.
cr_nasil_h2: Press, talk, hear it in your helmet.
cr_k_h2: This is how you talk to it.
cr_d1_q: How far to go? Is it going to rain on the way?
cr_d1_a: Checking. About 1 hour 58 minutes left. It’s raining right now, with more light rain ahead in about an hour.
cr_d1_q2: What time do I get there?
cr_d2_q: Any good coffee place on the way?
cr_d2_a: There’s one 18 miles ahead, on your right, with a high rating. Want me to add it as a stop?
cr_d3_a: Switching to back roads, calculating the route.
cr_d4_q: Will my fuel get me there?
cr_d4_a: Yes: your range is about 130 miles, and the destination is 87 miles away.
cr_d5_q: Tell the group we’re stopping for a break.
cr_d5_a: Done. I told the group we’re taking a break.
cr_d6_q: Remind me to oil the chain tomorrow.
cr_d6_a: Okay. I’ll tell you first thing when you open me tomorrow.
cr_k_not: The examples are written for illustration. Solid labels are the status labels the app shows on screen; dashed ones don’t appear on screen, they only describe what happens.
cr_y_p: Grouped into five. You don’t have to memorise any of them; just say what you want in your own words.
cr_g1_p: It fixes the route for you.
cr_g1_l:
• Adds a stop, removes one or skips the next
  • Changes the destination and puts the stops in order
  • Switches between back roads and the shortest route
  • Shows the route on the map, takes you home
cr_g2_p: It searches along your route and around you.
cr_g2_l:
• Finds fuel, food or coffee ahead and names the best rated first
  • Looks for somewhere to stay tonight
  • Tells you the time left, the next turn and where you are
  • Tells you if there are sharp bends or climbs ahead
cr_g3_p: What you ask before and during the ride.
cr_g3_l:
• What the weather will be like, whether it rains on your route
  • Checks the rain radar and opens it on the map
  • How far your tank will go, whether there’s fuel on the way
  • The rain radar works only in the US and Germany. For range, enter once in Settings the distance you rode on a full tank.
cr_g4_p: When a group ride is on.
cr_g4_l:
• Tells you where everyone is and who has fallen behind
  • Sends the group a ready-made alert: I’m behind, break, danger, fuel
  • If you shared the route with the group, it asks who a change applies to
cr_g5_p: While your hands stay on the bars.
cr_g5_l:
• Starts and ends navigation
  • Starts and stops ride recording
  • Finds someone in your contacts; one tap on the screen places the call
  • Keeps a note you ask for, deletes it if you say “forget”
  • Raises or lowers its own volume: “turn it up”
cr_m_h2: One does the job, the other talks.
cr_m_p: Just say “open chat mode” while you talk.
cr_m1_d: It knows your route and gets things done.
cr_m1_l:
• Any fuel on the way?
  • Where are the others?
  • Let’s take the back roads.
  • What will the weather be?
  • Take me home.
cr_m2_d: You pick the topic; it remembers earlier chats.
cr_m2_l:
• Let’s practise English.
  • Let’s plan the day together.
  • Tell me a story.
  • Where did we stop yesterday?
cr_ses_p: Listen to each one in Settings and pick: Quartz, Tempo, Stone or Willow.
cr_t_p: The minutes you spend with AI CoRider come out of the time Pro renews and out of packs that never expire.
cr_t1_d: Your talk time resets to 10 minutes every 30 days.
cr_t2_d: You can talk for 5 minutes during the trial.
cr_t3_d: 30, 60 or 180 minutes. They never expire and don’t vanish at month end; Chat mode opens with them too.
cr_p1_h: It works when you start it
cr_p1_d: The microphone opens only when you tap the AI CoRider button on the map.
cr_p2_d: Your voice isn’t recorded by us. It goes to a third-party cloud voice service to produce the answer.
cr_p3_d: Only text, such as the distance left and the next manoeuvre, leaves the route.
cr_p4_d: The notes you ask it to keep are stored on your phone; say “forget” and they’re deleted.
cr_f1_a: No. There’s no wake word. The microphone opens only when you tap the AI CoRider button on the map. The session closes when you end it, after a stretch of silence, or when navigation ends.
cr_f2_a: No. What you say goes to a cloud voice service to produce the answer, so AI CoRider needs an internet connection. Without one, a session can’t start.
cr_f3_a: It answers in the language you speak. There are no commands to learn; say it in your own words.
cr_f4_q: What happens when my talk time runs out?
cr_f4_a: Pro renews 10 minutes every 30 days, and the free trial includes 5. If that isn’t enough, add a 30, 60 or 180 minute pack that never expires.
cr_f5_q: What’s the difference between Planner and Chat?
cr_f5_a: Planner knows your route and gets things done: it adds stops, finds places and changes the route, and it’s included in Pro. In Chat you pick the topic and it remembers earlier chats; it opens with a minute pack.
cr_f6_q: Does everyone in a group hear it, and whose minutes are used?
cr_f6_a: If you call AI CoRider into the group intercom, everyone in the room hears it. The minutes come from the account of whoever called it.
cr_f7_q: I ask if my fuel will last, but it gives no range. Why?
cr_f7_a: For range, enter once in Settings the distance you rode on a full tank. Until you do, AI CoRider doesn’t guess; it tells you so.
cr_f8_q: Do I need Bluetooth to hear it in my helmet?
cr_f8_a: If your helmet is connected to the phone over Bluetooth, the voice comes through it; otherwise it plays from the phone. Can’t hear it in the wind? Just say “turn it up”.
